narrative.overview: Pikonoid looks as if its entire world were authored inside a constrained console cartridge: every mark lands on the pixel grid, every color has a named role, and depth comes from deliberate one-pixel bands rather than modern effects.
keyCharacteristics: Native 256x240 composition with integer-only scaling across 33 stages.
Opaque fixed-palette colors; no smooth alpha transitions.
Hard-edged geometry and one-pixel highlight/shadow bands.
Dense gameplay framed by cartridge-black negative space.

rules.name: The Opaque Palette Rule
rules.body: Gameplay effects move through named colors in discrete steps; they never dissolve through continuous alpha fades.

rules.name: The Cartridge Copy Rule
rules.body: Keep visible text uppercase and action-oriented; instructions name the logical action, not one device-specific key.

rules.name: The No Soft Light Rule
rules.body: Do not add glows, blur shadows, gradients, or semi-transparent overlays. If an object needs depth, draw another hard pixel.

dos: Do align positions, motion artifacts, and decorative marks to whole pixels.
Do reuse the rail, starfield, masthead, and fixed palette across every state.
Do express feedback through color steps, frame swaps, and discrete motion.
Do keep instructions device-neutral by naming mapped actions.
donts: Don't use copied ROM data, extracted game assets, or exact legacy layouts.
Don't add gradients, glass, blur, antialiasing, or continuous alpha fades.
Don't introduce rounded cards, stock fonts, or modern dashboard patterns.
Don't let interface chrome compete with the playfield.
